question.text: Bhageerathi Debt AIF (Cat II) holds a INR 1,000 par value debenture with 10% annual coupon, 5 years to maturity. Required yield = 12%. PVA(12%,5) = 3.605; PV(12%,5) = 0.567. What is the debenture's value?

explanation.text: The Logic: Annual coupon = 10% x 1000 = INR 100. Value = 100 x PVA(12%,5) + 1000 x PV(12%,5) = 100 x 3.605 + 1000 x 0.567 = 360.5 + 567 = INR 927.5 ~ INR 928. The bond sells at a discount because required yield (12%) > coupon (10%). The Trap: INR 1,000 assumes par (which is only true when required yield = coupon); INR 1,075 mis-signs the discount (it is a premium, but yield > coupon implies discount); INR 972 is an off-by-one factor error. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers identical bond math. Series-VII (Securities Operations) tests same formula. XV tests duration/convexity extensions which are out of XIX-D scope. Manager's Pro-Tip: Cat II debt AIFs must mark-to-model unlisted debentures using their YTM, not coupon rate. Show your independent valuer the yield curve of comparable-rated listed corporate bonds to justify your assumed YTM — IPEV Section 6 (debt valuation) specifically endorses this cash-flow discounting approach.
